lines.text: You went down. The box was empty.
Day six. For the first time, nothing can reach you.
lines.cap:
DAY 6. FOR THE FIRST TIME,
NOTHING CAN REACH YOU.

lines.text: And that's what it costs you. You stop checking.
lines.cap:
THAT'S WHAT IT COSTS YOU.
YOU STOP CHECKING.

lines.text: A moving train. Nothing boards it above twenty miles an hour. That's physics.
lines.cap:
A MOVING TRAIN. NOTHING
BOARDS IT ABOVE 20 MPH.

lines.text: Rule one. Hold the dead-man's switch. Let go for sixty seconds, and the train stops itself.
lines.cap:
RULE 1. HOLD THE SWITCH.
LET GO, AND IT STOPS.

lines.text: So your thumb never leaves it.
Thirty-two carriages behind you. You checked eleven. The rest were sealed.
Rule two. Sleep in twenty-minute blocks. Never longer.
You set the timer. Twenty. Twenty. Twenty.
lines.cap:
YOU SET THE TIMER.
TWENTY. TWENTY. TWENTY.

lines.text: Radio. The loop, whole at last. Do not approach the cities. Transit south. Rig Bravo. Six-two south.
lines.cap:
THE LOOP, WHOLE AT LAST:
RIG BRAVO. SIX-TWO SOUTH.

lines.text: Rule three. Do not stop. For anything on the line.
lines.cap:
RULE 3. DO NOT STOP.
FOR ANYTHING ON THE LINE.

lines.text: A thousand miles of range. The coast in two days. You don't stop.
lines.cap:
1,000 MILES OF RANGE.
THE COAST IN TWO DAYS.

lines.text: Three oh two. You wake because the engine note has changed.
Your thumb is still on the switch. You never let go.
lines.cap:
YOUR THUMB IS STILL ON IT.
YOU NEVER LET GO.

lines.text: But the train is slowing. Forty. Thirty-one. Twenty-two.
Somebody pulled the emergency brake. From carriage thirty-two.
